newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Inquiry says crash cause lost with 73 soldiers.
newsitem.headline: Inquiry says crash cause lost with 73 soldiers.

text.p: An official Israeli inquiry concluded on Wednesday that no one would ever know what caused the mid-air crash of two helicopters in which 73 soldiers were killed in February.
But Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai said he would accept the recommendations of the five-man committee to take disciplinary action against four officers.

Analysts had said that with no in-flight recordings and no survivors, investigators would have a hard time determining what caused Israel's worst military air disaster -- the collision of two Sikorsky CH-53 helicopters.

"The commission, despite its best efforts, did not manage to reach clear and unequivocal conclusions as to the reasons for the accident," committee chairman David Ivri, a former air force chief, told a news conference.
"To our regret the truth was taken with the victims of the disaster to the hereafter, all the more since it's highly likely they were surprised and didn't understand what was happening," he added.
Security sources had said the helicopters were circling along Israel's northern border waiting for permission to cross into Lebanon when the rotor of one of the helicopters hit the tail of the other.
The disaster plunged the country into grief as nearly every Israeli could trace a connection to at least one of the victims.
The helicopters were flying to an occupation zone in Lebanon which Israel carved out in 1985 to repel guerrilla attacks on its northern frontier.

The committee recommended an administrative reprimand for a brigadier-general and a major. It also recommended that a lieutenant-colonel and another major be dismissed from their jobs and barred from command posts.
